claims.text: Conventional TOR-TILD uses traditional EAM reference potentials for free-energy integration.
Conventional EAM references inadequately represent the configurational space of the ab initio liquid.
The EAM reference should be replaced by an MLIP trained specifically on ab initio liquid-phase data.
Free-energy perturbation should be used in place of a purely thermodynamic-integration approach.
A liquid-trained MLIP captures a broader range of atomic configurations than an EAM model.
The liquid-trained MLIP will reproduce the ab initio liquid potential-energy surface better than the EAM reference.
Better reproduction of the ab initio potential-energy surface will enhance phase-space overlap between the reference and target states.
The MLIP-based free-energy perturbation steps will connect states having more similar atomic ensembles than the EAM-based TI path.
Greater phase-space overlap will improve convergence of free-energy estimates.
The MLIP approach will produce smaller free-energy differences along the integration path.
The MLIP approach will reduce TI path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references by at least a factor of two.
The proposed method is applicable to high-entropy alloys containing five or more elements.
The proposed method is applicable at temperatures close to and slightly above the alloys' melting points.
The magnitude of the mismatch reduction depends on the quality of the MLIP training dataset.
The magnitude of the mismatch reduction depends on alloy complexity and the investigated temperature range.
